questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The main reason for picking Geneva was that I wanted to practice my French.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I had a great time and I met some great people.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. They were quite informative via emails and such.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation session where I got loads of information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: As a 4eu+ student we got preferential access to student housing via the university, which was very helpful considering how expensive the private renting market is. So make sure you sign up for that and regularly check your email.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Overall, the housing options are fine - but the quality can differ. I would not recommend Hugo-de-senger as I got a moldy room, but thankfully I got moved to another place after complaining. From what I know, some good options are voisins, Epinettes, Champel, ansermet and candolle.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I think it depends on faculty, but in global studies institute we had a couple of weeks to try out some classes before we had to be signed up. Signing up was online, but you get information about the process at the orientation of the faculty.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Orientation session from each faculty

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The main thing you have to be aware of is that some faculties does not allow master students to take bachelor classes. Global studies institute, where I was enrolled, did not allow this, while the social science faculty did. So this may limit your options.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall, the courses had a much lower level and workload than the courses in Copenhagen. However, I think it depends on the faculty – the courses I took at the social science faculty were generally easier than those at the Global studies institute.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Similar in the sense that it was usually based lecture-based. However, some courses included mandatory student presentations as well. And some courses had no readings at all, which is of course very different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Émotions et résolution de conflit, Relations économiques entre l’Union Européenne et les Pays en Développement, Understanding global governance, Global Governance: The art of negotiation, Migrations transnationales, rapports sociaux de sexe, de classe et de race

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found 'Relations économiques entre l’Union Européenne et les Pays en Développement' very interesting and relevant for political science students. I also really enjoyed Global Governance: The art of negotiation, especially the exam which was a two day negotiation. There were also a lot of interesting people who gave lectures.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Having to pay 40 francs to get residence permit

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Swiss trains are very reliable but also very expensive! I bought a half-off pass for about 100 francs/year and it was very quickly payed off. So if you plan to travel a lot, that might be a good option.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of associations, sports, trips etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The ESN-network is great and hosts many cool trips and events. So definitely get involved in those!
I also went on a ski-trip to St. Moritz through UNIGE, which was great!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Skiing, hiking, swimming in the lake.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take courses in French.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Punctuality, especially of the public transport.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get involved in ESN, enjoy the beautiful landscape and make sure to get a head start on accommodation.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: People are generally very nice if you want to practice your French, even if your French is not perfect. However, most people speak English as well, so if you do not know any French, you can manage as well.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting great people and practicing my French

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having mold in my room and therefore having to switch, but it worked out pretty well in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
